title: Graph queries, correlated subqueries, and error handling
summary: Traverse graph data with MATCH, write correlated subqueries, and handle errors with TRY/CATCH and THROW.

items: Implement TRY...CATCH with THROW and transaction rollback.

blocks.body: This lesson bundles three exam skills: graph MATCH, correlated queries, and error handling.

terms.definition: Graph pattern-matching operator over NODE and EDGE tables.
A subquery that references columns from the outer query, evaluated per outer row.
Structured error handling block in T-SQL.

blocks.body: Graph: `SELECT ... FROM Person p, likes l, Person p2 WHERE MATCH(p-(l)->p2)`. Error handling: wrap DML in `BEGIN TRY ... END TRY BEGIN CATCH ... END CATCH`; use `THROW` (re-raises) or `RAISERROR`, and check `@@TRANCOUNT`/`XACT_STATE()` before rollback.

items.mistake: Committing inside CATCH without checking XACT_STATE().
items.fix: A doomed transaction (XACT_STATE = -1) can only be rolled back.

tips: THROW with no arguments re-raises the current error inside CATCH.
MATCH only works on NODE/EDGE tables.

blocks.body: Use MATCH for graph traversal, correlated subqueries for per-row logic, and TRY/CATCH + THROW for robust error handling.
